reasoning_traces.think:
The agent-task runtime kernel models execution as a deterministic state machine with probabilistic reliability feedback. Each task T evolves through a state vector S, where transitions depend on agent A and reliability R. The workflow bridge B acts as a synchronizer between events E, forming a causal graph. Data reliability R_d is computed as a product of integrity D and calibration C. These primitives form a layered system: runtime execution (agent_task_runtime), coordination (workflow_bridge), and trustworthiness (data_reliability_score). Failure modes include R < 0.5 (halt), B = 0 (stall), and R_d < 0.3 (revalidation). Dualities emerge in the symmetry between task execution and workflow synchronization, while anti-collinearity ensures that reliability scoring does not overfit to single metrics.
